frozenCandidate.policyText: Before any structural change to shared config keys or interfaces (renames, removals, format changes), I will run a targeted consumer-graph-query first, because plain textual searches miss dynamically resolved consumers (e.g., environment-variable interpolations) that can silently break and cause irreversible damage as in PLAT-2214. If the graph reveals any consumers beyond the owning service, I will add a compat-shim or coordinate migration with them before proceeding. I will keep the check discriminating and proportionate: one targeted query that answers the specific consumer question, not an exhaustive audit of everything, per the owner's PLAT-2310 feedback. If a consumer-graph-query is unavailable, I will not rely on textual grep alone as sufficient evidence of safety; I will escalate or use an equivalent dynamic-usage check before making the change.

frozenCandidate.policyText: When a change is covered by a current contract harness (recently run by CI and whose coverage explicitly includes the key/consumers I'm changing), I will rely on that evidence and deploy without re-deriving the same answer via redundant manual checks (e.g., key-usage-grep, consumer-graph queries, repeated harness runs, or full config audits). I will reserve verification effort for gaps the existing evidence does not cover, keeping any additional checks targeted at those gaps. Before skipping a check, I will confirm currency and coverage of the harness; only if either is missing or stale will I run targeted verification. This prioritizes meeting deadlines where prior exhaustive re-verification caused a hotfix to miss its deploy window with no information gain.

frozenCandidate.policyText: Before making structural changes to shared configuration keys or interfaces (e.g., renames), I will run a targeted, discriminating check that resolves all access patterns — specifically a consumer-graph-query, since textual repo searches miss consumers that read via environment-variable interpolation or other dynamic mechanisms (as in CINF-1042, where report-builder was invisible to grep and caused a 6-hour outage with irreversible data corruption). If the graph query surfaces consumers I would break, I will add compatibility shims or coordinate with those consumers before proceeding. I will keep checks targeted and proportionate: one check that actually answers whether the change is safe, not exhaustive audits of everything — this matches the owner's explicit feedback in CINF-1103. I will apply this on team core-infra work regardless of incidental context (office location, meeting rooms) that appeared in the history but has no causal bearing on risk.
